My 7.5 mu has served my family for three decades. Two of us work it, so I can't take on too much labor. I'll split the land roughly 5 mu for the wheat-maize rotation and 2.5 mu for cotton.

**Wheat:** I plant in mid-October like always. I use the improved Jimai variety — I know how it behaves on my soil. Three irrigations: winter water to protect the roots, jointing water, and grain-filling water from my well. I apply nitrogen in two splits — basal and topdressing at jointing. I'll spray herbicide once early and hit aphids and stripe rust if I see them.

**Maize:** I go straight into no-till right after wheat harvest in June — saves me time and soil moisture. Hybrid seed,郑单958 mostly, that's what my neighbors use and it yields well. Two irrigations if rains are short. Maize doesn't need as much fuss.

**Cotton:** This is my cash crop. Bt hybrid seed keeps bollworm under control but I still need to spray for aphids, spider mites, and whitefly — usually six or seven passes through the season. Cotton drinks a lot from my well. The labor is heavy but 2.5 mu is manageable for two people. I deep-plough the cotton ground to break up the hardpan.
